source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter III, §17 Attacking without the Aid of Knights, Example 44

steps.title: What Black feared
steps.source: Black's last move was P - K 6, played with the object of stopping what he thought was White's threat, viz.: R - Q R 5, to which he would have answered Q - B 5 ch and drawn the game by perpetual check.

narration.say: Black's last move was e3. He feared Ra5, and planned to answer with Qf4 check and perpetual check.
But White has a more forceful move, and mates in three.

feedback.*: The rook on b7 takes a pawn with check.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Mate in three: start with a sacrifice.
exercise.wrong: The rook on b7 takes a pawn with check.
exercise.success: 1. Rxa7, check! The queen must take.

narration.say: Now the move Black feared comes with more force.

feedback.*: The other rook goes to the a-file, behind your queen.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Line up against the black queen.
exercise.wrong: The other rook goes to the a-file, behind your queen.
exercise.success: 2. Ra5. Whatever Black does, White mates next move. Say Black plays Rb7.

feedback.*: Capture the rook that just moved to b7.

exercise.prompt: White to move and give checkmate in one.
exercise.wrong: Capture the rook that just moved to b7.
